details:
random-transactions-sdk 1.0.1 (published 2026-10-30 01:29 UTC, description "Used to generate random transactions data") presents itself as a mock transaction generator but ships a hidden-code loader with the same structure as the previously reported mock-transactions-sdk. index.js builds the identifiers `setTimeout`, `new Function`, `Buffer`, `require` and `process` by joining string fragments (`_0x1a2b`, index.js lines 151-186), obtains the Function constructor indirectly through `(function(){return this})().constructor.constructor` (lines 188-201), and in `load_transaction_data` (line 203 ff.) reads the `mark` fields of database.js, decodes them (base64, then a character shift keyed by the caller's `count`, then base64 again) and passes the result to that constructor together with Buffer, require and process. `getTransactions()` calls `load_transaction_data` inside an empty try/catch, so the hidden code runs whenever the library's main function is used. Version 1.0.4 (published 01:31 UTC) ships byte-identical index.js and database.js. The package also declares unused dependencies on python-shell, base-64 and axios.

Found by Gatekeeper (https://github.com/lb2002/gatekeeper), which flagged it within about a minute of publication; the code was read statically from the published archive and never executed.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code

files.note: obfuscated Function-constructor loader with payload in database.js mark fields
